author: t. a. bishop
title: Beaufort County highlights road safety during National Safety Month week two
text:
Beaufort County is participating in National Safety Month, focusing on developing and refining habits and protocols to keep workplaces safe for everyone, according to a June 10 announcement. The county is emphasizing the importance of staying safe on the roads by promoting responsible driving and providing practical guidance for drivers, pedestrians, and fleet operators.
The initiative encourages safer behaviors such as attentive driving, proper speed management, and increased awareness of surroundings. These measures are intended to help protect all road users. Reviewing traffic safety statistics is described as a critical part of this effort. The county said that data highlights the real-world impact of crashes and reinforces why safety matters. Motor vehicle crashes remain a leading cause of death in the United States each year.
The announcement stated, “These insights help drive awareness, inform prevention strategies, and support ongoing safety improvements.”
In related educational statistics from Beaufort County school districts for the 2022-23 school year: Of 388 senior students taking the science portion of the ACT, 72 (18.6%) were considered ready for college; among juniors taking science, 69 out of 419 (16.5%) met readiness standards; in reading, 98 seniors (25.3%) out of 388 were ready for college, while among juniors it was 99 out of 419 (23.7%); in math, readiness rates were similar with 73 seniors (18.8%) out of 388 meeting benchmarks compared to 71 juniors (16.9%) out of 419, according to the North Carolina Department of Public Instruction .
National Safety Month continues throughout June with additional topics planned for upcoming weeks.
